Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, Equestrian Committee Members will be participating via
teleconference. Committee meetings are recorded for minutes preparation purposes.

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:
966 0484 6350, Meeting Password: 461244. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call-in
option from a phone line.)

- Public correspondence may be emailed to Cynthia Morquecho, Community Services Supervisor at
cynthiam@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded
to the Committee Members for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment”
button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After
you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
public, will be considered by the Committee and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by
entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 966 0484 6350, Meeting Password: 461244. Members of the public
who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following process: After
joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the lower portion of your
screen. The Meeting Host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the agenda you would like to
speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city/agendas.

REGULAR EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE
  MEETING MINUTES
  APRIL 26, 2021

A regular meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by CHAIR HUFF at 7:01 p.m.

Committee Members Present:  Huff, Silvano, Shinn, Nilsen, Brtis, Ciarolla, Robinson,
  Griggs, Harik, Zigrang,

Committee Members Absent:  Martin

City Staff Present:  Maintenance Superintendent, Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor, Cynthia Morquecho

DRAFT MINUTES OF MARCH 22, 2021

MEMBER ZIGRANG moved, seconded by MEMBER BRTIS, to:

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE MARCH 22, 2021 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF so ordered.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

None.

STAFF ITEMS

  A. COVID-19 UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

Supervisor Morquecho stated that COVID case numbers continue to decline. Less restrictions as
we have moved into the orange tier. We have received some guidance on small gatherings and
under this we believe we can begin approving park permits under 100 people as well as horse
shows. We continue to evaluate protocols under events and gatherings.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF received and filed the report.

  B. EQUESTRIAN FEE REVIEW

Supervisor Morquecho provided a brief review of the staff report. MEMBER SILVANO suggested
that the fees remain unchained due to the 2020 COVID year. CHAIR HUFF stated that because
there has not been an increase in maintenance costs it is suggested to keep fees as is as a
courtesy to the equestrian community.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  1
APRIL 26, 2021
   COMMITTEE MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
  BRTIS, to recommend to the Park and Activities Commission for FY 2021-22
  or calendar year 2021 (Horse Trainers Business License tax and Public Arena Use
  Permit fees).

  AYES: Huff, Silvano, Shinn, Nilsen, Brtis, Ciarolla, Robinson, Griggs, Harik, Zigrang,
  ABSENT: Martin

  Motion carries.

  C. FOURTH OF JULY SAFETY CONCERNS (VERBAL REPORT)

Supervisor Morquecho stated that staff will be meeting with the Sheriff’s Department to discuss
any fire and safety concerns during the month of July. She added that staff would like to hear
any concerns from the Committee. MEMBER SHINN stated that in the past there have been
safety concerns in both the landfill and city trails. MEMBER SHINN suggested more Sheriff on
patrol during the week of 4th of July. Supervisor Morquecho stated that she would take the
comments and concerns to the Sheriff representative and will follow up with an update to the
Equestrian Committee.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF received and filed the report.

  D. MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE (VERBAL REPORT)

Supervisor Morquecho stated that staff is planning the event and has determined that postponing
would be the best option. There may be some modifications in place to meet any County
restrictions during the time of the event. Staff has coordinated with the Mayor and has decided to
postpone the event to July. She added that it was suggested to host the Mayor’s Ride event
closer to the 4th of July holiday last year and asked for suggestions from the Committee as to a
possible date change. COMMITTEE MEMBERS agreed that the date postponement would be a
good option.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF received and filed the report.

  E. HORSE SHOW AND SPECIAL EVENTS UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

Supervisor Morquecho stated that as the County moves through the tier system, restrictions have
been loosened on group gatherings and events. Currently, the County has opened up for group
gathering of up to 100 people. Which has allowed for the City to open to horse shows. Staff
continues to discuss with County representatives the upcoming changes to events as we are
looking to move into the yellow tier. Additionally, some of the City Annual events have been
postponed including the Tracy Austin Tournament, and Mayor’s Breakfast Ride. MEMBER
CIAROLLA asked if the City plans to implement no masks for vaccinated people during events
and group gatherings. Supervisor Morquecho responded that the City will continue to stay in line
with County protocols which at this time is still requiring masks outdoors at all times.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF received and filed the report.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  2
APRIL 26, 2021
   F. HORSE TRAINER BUSINESS LICENSE LIST (VERBAL REPORT)

Supervisor Morquecho stated that staff recently received the latest updated list for registered
horse trainers with the most up to date list totaling 19 registered trainers She explained that
typically there will be a virtual trainers meeting held on May 11th, 2021. New lists have been
posted at all arenas. Supervisor Morquecho added that the list of registered trainers will now be
provided on the City’s equestrian section website and will continuously be updated ever quarter.
MEMBER GRIGGS stated a spelling error on a trainer name KOCH. Supervisor Morquecho noted
the error and stated that the list will be updated with the suggested edit.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF received and filed the report.

  G. EQUESTRIAN LOG

Community Member Tiffany Chiu stated that she would like to understand why there has been
closure of a gate on the unincorporated area of City trails. Superintendent Goldsmith stated that
the area referenced is owned by the County and therefore the City does not control trail closures
there.

MEMBER GRIGGS stated that there is a person that comes to Ernie Howlett Park in the mornings
with a goat off leash and is walking with the goat on the trails. MEMBER GRIGGS asked if there
were any City regulations in place that would require him to leash the goat as it can scare horses
on the trail. Supervisor Morquecho stated that currently the park regulations does require all
animals to be leashed while in the park space. Superintendent Goldsmith stated that he would
try talking to the gentleman about the concern. MEMBER ROBINSON asked who enforces city
code requirements. Superintendent Goldsmith stated that staff typically tries to address the issue
first, then escalates the issue to the City Code Compliance Officer. If City staff is unable to resolve
from Code Compliance, then the issue may be escalated to the Sheriff’s Department.

MEMBER GRIGGS stated that another issue she has encountered is the trails being used in the
evening by a trail riding company out of the PV stables. She is concerned that they are using the
trails frequently. Neighbors have asked if anything can be done to prevent such a large group
horse rider from coming through the area so frequently. MEMBER SILVANO stated that she does
not think regulating horse businesses was a good idea. She added that she would like to see
more horse activities taking place. MEMBER NILSEN added that she agrees with MEMBER
SILVANO and that the City should not prevent horse activity in the area. MEMBER GRIGGS
added that the concern came from a report that a rider was almost bucked off of a horse.
Supervisor Morquecho stated that the City is aware of the trail riding group and has reached out
to make sure that the group is aware of the City’s business license requires. Additionally, she
added that when a business license is obtained, they are required to provide proof of insurance
for any type of injury that may occur on the public trails.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF received and filed the report.

COMMITTEE REPORTS

  A.  ADOPT-A- TRAIL
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  3
APRIL 26, 2021
 MEMBER SILVANO thanked Superintendent Goldsmith for the work done to prepare for the day
camp event.

MEMBER BRTIS stated that sewer company created a hole on the Palomino trail and have
covered it with a safety cone. Superintendent Goldsmith stated that he was unaware of that and
would investigate the issue. MEMBER BRTIS added that there is a real safety concern as most
people like to gallop up the trail and could easily miss the safety cone. Superintendent Goldsmith
stated that they are inspecting all the storm drain systems and he would reach out to the company
to about the issue.

MEMBER NILSEN stated that in a previous equestrian meeting a discussion took place regarding
the Chandler Park playground proposal. MEMBER NILSEN added that she had not heard any
movement on the project and wanted to be sure that the Equestrian Committee was represented
in any future conversations on the project proposal. Additionally, MEMBER NILSEN stated that
she volunteered for the Chandler Park Playground subcommittee and would like to be included
in any future meeting notification. Supervisor Morquecho apologized for the miscommunication
and stated that there have been meetings held with the playground subcommittee and community
outreach was done to gage interest in the proposal. Additionally, there will be future
subcommittee meetings and staff will include MEMBER NILSEN in the meeting updates.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

A. COMMITTEE T-SHIRTS
B. YOUTH AMBASSADOR PROGRAM
